page.layout: One printed page, one column of running text. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Below the text a centred chapter heading "CAP. XXIIII." with an italic title of four lines. Signature at the lower right of the text. No margin notes.

main_text.p: tio enim quodam modo intelligit. Quod au-tem hoc modo cognoscit aliud esse potest, quàm est, & unum contrariorum in eo esse debet. Propterea existimauit Aristoteles patibilem mentem unà cum corpore extingui, & eam, quae agens est, separabilem esse & aeternam. Quamobrem his addit ipsam causam se cognoscere, & separabilem esse, cui omnino nullum est contrarium. Sed utraque mens (meo iudicio) forma non distinguitur, sed duntaxat opere & facultate. Postremò non omnis intellectio vera est & falsa, sed ea duntaxat, quae aliquid de aliquo dicit, & enunciatio dicitur. Affirmatio huiusmodi est, & omnis vera esse, aut falsa perhibetur. Sed nō omnis intellectio huiusmodi est. Ea enim duntaxat vera est, qua quid sit res mete concipitur, & cuius forma intelligitur. Ac quem-admodum proprij subiecti semper visus actu verus est, ita intellectio eorum omnium, quae materia carent semper vera. Postrema autē metis intellectio syllogismus est, quo aliquid verum esse, aut falsum demonstramus.
main_text.head: CAP. XXIIII. Id in mente bonum & malum esse, quod in sensu dolor & voluptas. Quae-nam sit mentis actio practica?

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse page is present in the lower left and right and is left out. A small stray mark at the right edge is left out. Doubtful readings: "iudicio" is printed with a ligature-like form, read as iudicio [?] in the text was not marked because the reading is probable. "autē" is printed with a damaged vowel mark and may be autem or autē. The word "syllogismuseft" is printed run together; read as syllogismus est. The printed signature "Q 2" is partly obscured and the Q is stylised. Long s is set as plain s throughout.
